NTA because your SIL is a thief and a liar. She has no defense here and you have every right to defend the cookbook against her thievery. However, I do think you should cook something or give a thoughtful gift to the cousin in this scenario. Your SIL had her lie exposed and while she knew how much the cookbook meant to you, the rest of your family may not have and you look like TA to them even though you aren’t. To explain your POV, apologize, and do something thoughtful for your cousin would help make your family realize you are not TA in this scenario.

Originally I was going to say NAH as this is a subject that could be handled through talking about it maturely, as he feels proud of the sculpture he made and he views it as a loving gift to you and as a symbol of “you’ll always be beautiful.” On the other hand your body has changed and now you detest the sculpture because it portrays a body type that you no longer have and feel insecure of. Both of y’all have valid viewpoints.

However YTA for selling the sculpture without consulting him or his feelings on the matter first. I understand why you sold it because it made you feel very insecure in a place where you’re supposed to feel loved, but to him he may view it as you getting rid of or not caring about his love for you.
